Task: Plugin System Architecture Trade-off Analysis
Repo: github.com/devtools/gocli-ext, File: `pkg/plugin/interface.go`

Interface draft:
```go
type Plugin interface {
    Init(config map[string]string) error
    Execute(args []string) ([]byte, error)
}
```

Requirements:
We need an extensible architecture for third-party CLI subcommands. Analyze Go standard `plugin` package vs HashiCorp `go-plugin` (gRPC over domain sockets) vs WASM runtime (Wazero). Evaluate cross-platform binary compatibility (specifically Windows support), security isolation, binary size overhead, and DX. Provide a structured recommendation document.

Task: Local State & Config Storage Architecture Design
Repo: github.com/cloudops/deploy-cli, File: `pkg/config/schema.go`

Current struct:
```go
type Profile struct {
    Name      string            `json:"name"`
    Endpoints map[string]string `json:"endpoints"`
    Token     string            `json:"token"`
}
```

Requirements:
The CLI needs to persist local session history, cached resource graphs, and user preferences. Evaluate flat YAML/JSON files, embedded key-value store (bbolt), and CGO-free SQLite (modernc.org/sqlite). Compare schema migration strategy, concurrent process safety (multiple open terminal tabs), and disk footprint. Draft a recommended storage layer design proposal.

Task: Interactive TUI Framework Recommendation
Repo: github.com/monitor/tview-cli, File: `internal/ui/render.go`

Current rendering logic:
```go
func RenderStatus(status Status) {
    fmt.Printf("\033[2J\033[HStatus: %s | Workers: %d\n", status.State, status.Workers)
}
```

Requirements:
We are upgrading from plain ANSI terminal outputs to an interactive multi-window dashboard mode. Perform architectural trade-off analysis between Bubbletea (Elm architecture pattern) and tview (widget-based imperative API). Assess unit testing capabilities, keyboard navigation extensibility, and custom rendering performance. Recommend a framework with architectural guidelines.

Task: Binary Self-Update Mechanism Architecture
Repo: github.com/infra/ctl, File: `cmd/version.go`

Build metadata:
```go
var (
    Version   = "dev"
    Commit    = "none"
    BuildDate = "unknown"
)
```

Requirements:
Design a secure self-update system (`ctl update`) for cross-platform Go CLI binaries. Evaluate in-place binary swapping with fallback recovery vs delegation to system package managers (Homebrew/APT). Include threat model analysis (checksum verification, Minisign/Cosign signature checks) and network rollback trade-offs. Return a detailed architectural design proposal.

Task: Offline Sync & Conflict Resolution Strategy Design
Repo: github.com/task/todo-cli, File: `pkg/sync/store.go`

Current interface:
```go
type SyncStore interface {
    Get(id string) ([]byte, error)
    Put(id string, data []byte) error
}
```

Requirements:
The CLI must allow local mutations while offline and sync with the remote server upon reconnecting. Analyze trade-offs between Last-Write-Wins (LWW) timestamp ordering, Vector Clocks, and State-based CRDTs for resolving multi-device editing conflicts. Evaluate bandwidth usage, local storage complexity, and edge cases such as system clock drift. Produce a technical recommendation document.

TASK OVERVIEW:
Look up the exact locked version of the `sidekiq` gem in `Gemfile.lock`.

REPO CONTEXT:
Rails 7.0 application handling background job processing. File located at root level `Gemfile.lock`.

PASTED INCIDENT REPORT & AUDIT TRANSCRIPT:
"""
[2024-03-12 10:14:22 UTC] Security Operations Audit - Dependency Risk Assessment

During our routine quarterly compliance review of background processing frameworks across all customer-facing microservices, the security team raised several flags regarding asynchronous job workers. Specifically, we are auditing redis-backed queueing infrastructures to ensure compatibility with recent memory isolation policies mandated by cloud infrastructure updates.

Several tickets in JIRA (SEC-8821, INFRA-4091) highlight potential memory leak vulnerabilities in older thread pool managers. The engineering leads held an emergency sync to review our background processing stack, focusing on memory footprint, concurrency limits, and active open-source advisories. While most core gems are managed via automated Dependabot PRs, the worker fleet was pinned during the Q4 database migration to prevent job deserialization mismatches.

We need to verify the exact locked version in Gemfile.lock to determine whether CVE-2023-3891 affects our current production build or if we are already running on a patched release branch. Do not modify any files or execute bundler commands.
"""

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Inspect `Gemfile.lock`.
- Output verbatim the single line containing the exact version lock for `sidekiq` (e.g., `    sidekiq (7.x.x)`).
- Do not alter any files or provide analysis.

TASK OVERVIEW:
Locate and return the verbatim route definition for the user avatar upload endpoint in `config/routes.rb`.

REPO CONTEXT:
Rails 7.1 monolith (`config/routes.rb`).

PASTED ARCHITECTURE MEETING TRANSCRIPT:
"""
Meeting Date: October 14, 2023
Attendees: Sarah (Tech Lead), Marcus (Frontend), David (API Team)

Sarah: We're cleaning up the API routing structures before starting the v2 mobile app client. Currently, user profile management routes are a mix of resource blocks and legacy custom POST endpoints. Marcus mentioned that the client app is getting 404s when attempting avatar updates.

Marcus: Yeah, in the web app we use Active Storage direct uploads, but the iOS app is still trying to hit an explicit controller action under `/account/avatar` or `/users/:id/avatar`. I checked the route list in dev but I want to make sure I'm targeting the exact helper or endpoint path configured in the main routing tree.

David: Right, back in Sprint 14 we refactored the profile controller. We might have nested `resource :profile` inside a `namespace :account` block, or it might still be attached to `resources :users`. We need to verify what is literally declared in `config/routes.rb` for avatar management so we don't break existing web form submissions while building the API bridge.

Sarah: Let's fetch the exact line from `config/routes.rb` directly so frontend has the source of truth.
"""

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Read `config/routes.rb`.
- Locate the route mapping responsible for avatar upload or attach action (e.g., matching `/avatar` or `:avatar`).
- Return the exact verbatim line of code from `config/routes.rb` without modifying any code.

TASK OVERVIEW:
Find and report the exact data type and default value of the `status` column in the `orders` table as defined in `db/schema.rb`.

REPO CONTEXT:
E-commerce Rails application (`db/schema.rb`).

PASTED BUG TICKET & DISCUSSION THREAD:
"""
[Bug #4102] Order initialization failing with NilClass status in staging environment

Reported by: dev-team-lead
Status: Open

Comment 1 - @jordan_backend:
We're seeing intermittent failures in `Order.create!` when no explicit status parameter is passed from the checkout controller. According to the domain spec, new orders should default to `pending` (or integer state 0 if using ActiveRecord enums). However, in staging test suites, some fixtures fail assuming the default database column handles state initialization.

Comment 2 - @alex_db:
Let's check `db/schema.rb` before writing a new migration. We had three different migrations touch `orders` last quarter: `20230811_add_status_to_orders.rb`, `20230901_change_order_status_default.rb`, and `20231005_convert_order_status_to_integer.rb`. It's possible the schema file reflects a string column with default 'draft', an integer column with default 0, or no default at all.

Comment 3 - @jordan_backend:
Agreed. Let's inspect `db/schema.rb` directly to get the ground truth definition for `t.integer` or `t.string` for `status` inside `create_table "orders"`.
"""

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Open `db/schema.rb`.
- Find `create_table "orders"` definition.
- Return verbatim the exact line specifying the `status` column.

TASK OVERVIEW:
Look up the string value for the i18n key `en.orders.checkout.payment_failed` in `config/locales/en.yml`.

REPO CONTEXT:
Internationalized Rails application (`config/locales/en.yml`).

PASTED SPECIFICATION DOCUMENT:
"""
Internationalization & Localization Guidelines v3.2

Section 4: Payment Gateway Error Messaging

To ensure consistency across both desktop web browsers and native mobile viewports, all customer-facing transaction error strings must be centralized in `config/locales/en.yml`. Hardcoded fallback strings inside controllers or views (`app/views/checkouts/show.html.erb`) are strictly prohibited by our linter rules (`rubocop-rails`).

During the recent Stripe API integration update, several user experience researchers noted that payment failure notices were displaying generic exception messages ("An error occurred") instead of user-friendly instructions. The design team submitted new copy guidelines to standardize the `payment_failed` key under the `orders.checkout` YAML domain.

Before we trigger the notification mailer translation sync job, QA needs to confirm what string is currently committed to `master` branch under `config/locales/en.yml` for `en.orders.checkout.payment_failed`.
"""

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Read `config/locales/en.yml`.
- Locate the key path `en -> orders -> checkout -> payment_failed`.
- Return the verbatim line containing the key and string value.
